entries.statement: {p q : ℕ} → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q → Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ
entries.source:
/-- The **common part** `Λ Φ Λᵀ` of the factor covariance — the variance of `x` explained by
the latent factors (`BKM` Eq. (3.12), left summand; at `Φ = I` this is `Λ Λ′`). -/
noncomputable def commonCovariance (P : FactorParams p q) : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ :=
  P.loading * P.factorCov * P.loadingᵀ
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.commonCovariance
entries.doc:
The **common part** `Λ Φ Λᵀ` of the factor covariance — the variance of `x` explained by
the latent factors (`BKM` Eq. (3.12), left summand; at `Φ = I` this is `Λ Λ′`).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.IsStandardized P → ∀ (i : Fin p), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.commonCovariance P i i = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.communality P i
entries.source:
/-- For standardized factors the diagonal of the common part **is** the communality. -/
theorem commonCovariance_diag_eq_communality (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: BKM's normalization y ∼ N_q(0, I); BKM Eq. (3.2)
    (hP : IsStandardized P) (i : Fin p) :
    commonCovariance P i i = communality P i := by
  rw [commonCovariance_eq, hP, Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.mul_apply, communality]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => by rw [Matrix.transpose_apply, sq]
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.commonCovariance_diag_eq_communality
entries.doc: For standardized factors the diagonal of the common part **is** the communality.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.commonCovariance P = P.loading * P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose
entries.source:
theorem commonCovariance_eq (P : FactorParams p q) :
    commonCovariance P = P.loading * P.factorCov * P.loadingᵀ := rfl
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.commonCovariance_eq

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}, IsUnit A.det → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.commonCovariance (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.rotateParams P A) = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.commonCovariance P
entries.source:
/-- **The common part is rotation invariant**: `(Λ A)(A⁻¹ Φ A⁻ᵀ)(Λ A)ᵀ = Λ Φ Λᵀ`
(`BKM` §2.11, Eq. (2.26)). -/
theorem commonCovariance_rotateParams (P : FactorParams p q)
    {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}
    -- USER-INPUT: the reparameterization is a change of basis of the latent space;
    -- BKM §2.11
    (hA : IsUnit A.det) :
    commonCovariance (rotateParams P A) = commonCovariance P := by
  have h2 : (A⁻¹)ᵀ * Aᵀ = 1 := by
    rw [← Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.mul_nonsing_inv _ hA, Matrix.transpose_one]
  simp only [commonCovariance, rotateParams_loading, rotateParams_factorCov,
    Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.mul_assoc]
  rw [Matrix.mul_nonsing_inv_cancel_left _ _ hA, ← Matrix.mul_assoc (A⁻¹)ᵀ, h2,
    Matrix.one_mul]
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.commonCovariance_rotateParams
entries.doc:
**The common part is rotation invariant**: `(Λ A)(A⁻¹ Φ A⁻ᵀ)(Λ A)ᵀ = Λ Φ Λᵀ`
(`BKM` §2.11, Eq. (2.26)).

entries.statement: {p q : ℕ} → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q → Fin p → ℝ
entries.source:
/-- The **communality** `hᵢ² = ∑ⱼ λᵢⱼ²` of observed coordinate `i` — the part of its variance
explained by the common factors, for standardized factors (`BKM` p. 49, after Eq. (3.10)).

*Edge behavior:* the formula is the sum of squared loadings whatever `Φ` is; it equals the
common part `(Λ Φ Λᵀ)ᵢᵢ` of the variance exactly when `Φ = I`
(`commonCovariance_diag_eq_communality`). -/
noncomputable def communality (P : FactorParams p q) (i : Fin p) : ℝ :=
  ∑ k, (P.loading i k) ^ 2
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.communality
entries.doc:
The **communality** `hᵢ² = ∑ⱼ λᵢⱼ²` of observed coordinate `i` — the part of its variance
explained by the common factors, for standardized factors (`BKM` p. 49, after Eq. (3.10)).

*Edge behavior:* the formula is the sum of squared loadings whatever `Φ` is; it equals the
common part `(Λ Φ Λᵀ)ᵢᵢ` of the variance exactly when `Φ = I`
(`commonCovariance_diag_eq_communality`).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.IsStandardized P → P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef → ∀ (i : Fin p), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P i i = 1 → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.communality P i ≤ 1
entries.source:
/-- For **standardized observed variables** — the correlation-matrix scaling in which factor
analysis is usually reported — the communality is at most `1`. -/
theorem communality_le_one (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: BKM's normalization y ∼ N_q(0, I); BKM Eq. (3.2)
    (hP : IsStandardized P)
    -- USER-INPUT: a genuine specific-factor covariance; BKM Eq. (3.1)
    (hΨ : P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef)
    (i : Fin p)
    -- USER-INPUT: the observed variable `i` is standardized (Σ is a correlation matrix);
    -- BKM §3.4
    (hSig : factorCovariance P i i = 1) :
    communality P i ≤ 1 := by
  rw [← hSig]
  exact communality_le_variance P hP hΨ i
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.communality_le_one
entries.doc:
For **standardized observed variables** — the correlation-matrix scaling in which factor
analysis is usually reported — the communality is at most `1`.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.IsStandardized P → P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef → ∀ (i : Fin p), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.communality P i ≤ StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P i i
entries.source:
/-- The communality never exceeds the variance it decomposes (`BKM` Eq. (3.10) with
`ψᵢ ≥ 0`). -/
theorem communality_le_variance (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: BKM's normalization y ∼ N_q(0, I); BKM Eq. (3.2)
    (hP : IsStandardized P)
    -- USER-INPUT: a genuine specific-factor covariance; BKM Eq. (3.1)
    (hΨ : P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef) (i : Fin p) :
    communality P i ≤ factorCovariance P i i := by
  rw [variance_eq_communality_add_specificVariance P hP i]
  linarith [specificVariance_nonneg P hΨ i]
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.communality_le_variance
entries.doc:
The communality never exceeds the variance it decomposes (`BKM` Eq. (3.10) with
`ψᵢ ≥ 0`).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) (i : Fin p), 0 ≤ StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.communality P i
entries.source:
/-- Communalities are nonnegative (a sum of squares). -/
theorem communality_nonneg (P : FactorParams p q) (i : Fin p) : 0 ≤ communality P i :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => sq_nonneg _
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.communality_nonneg
entries.doc: Communalities are nonnegative (a sum of squares).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) {Q : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}, Q * Q.transpose = 1 → ∀ (i : Fin p), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.communality (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.rotateParams P Q) i = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.communality P i
entries.source:
/-- **Communalities are rotation invariant** — the classical reason communalities, unlike
loadings, are reportable quantities (`BKM` §2.11 with Eq. (3.10)). -/
theorem communality_rotateParams_orthogonal (P : FactorParams p q)
    {Q : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}
    -- USER-INPUT: `Q` is orthogonal; BKM §2.11, Eq. (2.24)
    (hQ : Q * Qᵀ = 1) (i : Fin p) :
    communality (rotateParams P Q) i = communality P i := by
  -- the communality is the `(i, i)` entry of `Λ Λᵀ`, which orthogonal rotation preserves
  have key : ∀ M : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin q) ℝ, ∑ k, (M i k) ^ 2 = (M * Mᵀ) i i := by
    intro M
    simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply, sq]
  rw [communality, communality, key, key, rotateParams_loading,
    loading_mul_transpose_rotateParams_orthogonal P hQ]
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.communality_rotateParams_orthogonal
entries.doc:
**Communalities are rotation invariant** — the classical reason communalities, unlike
loadings, are reportable quantities (`BKM` §2.11 with Eq. (3.10)).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), P.factorCov.PosSemidef → P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef → (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P).PosDef → (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)).compProd (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorScoreKernel P) = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorJointLaw P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)
entries.source:
/-- **HEADLINE — factor scores as an exact disintegration** (`BKM` Eq. (3.6)): the observed
law composed with the factor-score kernel is the joint law of `(x, y)`. -/
theorem compProd_factorJointLaw (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: genuine covariance parameters; BKM Eq. (3.1)–(3.2)
    (hΦ : P.factorCov.PosSemidef) (hΨ : P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef)
    -- USER-INPUT: nondegenerate observed covariance Σ = ΛΦΛᵀ + Ψ — without it `Σ⁻¹` is the
    -- `Matrix.inv` junk value; BKM Eq. (3.6)
    (hSig : (factorCovariance P).PosDef) :
    factorLaw P (multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)
        ⊗ₘ factorScoreKernel P
      = factorJointLaw P (multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov)
          (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov) := by
  have h := MixedEffects.compProd_lmmJointLaw (factorDesign P) P.μ P.factorCov P.uniqueCov
    hΦ hΨ hSig
  rw [factorDesign_X, toEuclideanLin_one_apply] at h
  rw [factorLaw_eq_lmmLaw, factorJointLaw, factorScoreKernel]
  exact h
entries.result: (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)).compProd (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorScoreKernel P) = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorJointLaw P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.compProd_factorJointLaw
entries.doc:
**HEADLINE — factor scores as an exact disintegration** (`BKM` Eq. (3.6)): the observed
law composed with the factor-score kernel is the joint law of `(x, y)`.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), P.factorCov.transpose = P.factorCov → StatLean.StatisticalModels.condCovMatrix (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P) (P.loading * P.factorCov) P.factorCov = P.factorCov - P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose * (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)⁻¹ * P.loading * P.factorCov
entries.source:
/-- **The posterior covariance is `Φ − Φ Λᵀ Σ⁻¹ Λ Φ`** — the Schur complement of the factor
model's joint covariance (`BKM` Eq. (3.6), Schur form). -/
theorem condCovMatrix_factorScores (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: symmetric latent covariance; BKM Eq. (3.2)
    (hΦ : P.factorCovᵀ = P.factorCov) :
    condCovMatrix (factorCovariance P) (P.loading * P.factorCov) P.factorCov
      = P.factorCov
        - P.factorCov * P.loadingᵀ * (factorCovariance P)⁻¹ * P.loading * P.factorCov := by
  simp only [condCovMatrix, Matrix.transpose_mul, hΦ, Matrix.mul_assoc]
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.condCovMatrix (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P) (P.loading * P.factorCov) P.factorCov = P.factorCov - P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose * (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)⁻¹ * P.loading * P.factorCov
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.condCovMatrix_factorScores
entries.doc:
**The posterior covariance is `Φ − Φ Λᵀ Σ⁻¹ Λ Φ`** — the Schur complement of the factor
model's joint covariance (`BKM` Eq. (3.6), Schur form).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) (F : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))) [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure F], StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.HasDiagonalUniqueness P → P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef → ∀ {i j : Fin p}, i ≠ j → StatLean.StatisticalModels.GraphicalModels.CondIndep (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.latentObsJointLaw P F (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)) (fun z => z.2.ofLp i) (fun z => z.2.ofLp j) Prod.fst
entries.source:
/-- **HEADLINE — local independence** (`BKM` §1.4, Eq. (1.9); linear-Gaussian instance §3.2,
Eq. (3.1)). In the Gaussian linear factor model with a **diagonal** specific-factor covariance
`Ψ`, two distinct observed coordinates are conditionally independent given the latent factor:
`xᵢ ⫫ xⱼ ∣ y` under the joint law of `(y, x)`.

This is the bridge between the two areas: the conclusion is `GraphicalModels.CondIndep`, the
disintegration predicate of the graphical slice, and the model is `FactorModels.latentObsJointLaw`.
The witnesses `CondIndep` asks for are the two coordinate marginals of the measurement kernel.

*Book vs Lean:* `BKM` Eq. (1.9) states local independence for the whole family and for an
arbitrary conditional density; here it is a **theorem** in the Gaussian linear model, in the
pairwise form that `CondIndep` can express. The family form is
`iIndepFun_eval_measurementKernel` / `map_measurementKernel_eq_pi`, stated at the kernel level
for want of a family conditional-independence predicate. -/
theorem condIndep_eval_latentObsJointLaw (P : FactorParams p q)
    (F : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)))
    -- LEAN-ONLY: the latent law is a probability measure — needed for `⊗ₘ` to be the joint law
    -- of a pair of random variables and for `Measure.fst_compProd` to return `F`
    [IsProbabilityMeasure F]
    -- USER-INPUT: the specific factors are uncorrelated across coordinates, i.e. `Ψ` diagonal;
    -- BKM §3.2 Eq. (3.1) — this is what makes Eq. (1.9) true here, and it is *not* enough
    -- without the Gaussianity built into the error law below
    (hΨdiag : HasDiagonalUniqueness P)
    -- USER-INPUT: `Ψ` is a genuine covariance matrix; BKM Eq. (3.1)
    (hΨ : P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef) {i j : Fin p}
    -- USER-INPUT: two distinct observed coordinates; BKM Eq. (1.9)
    (hij : i ≠ j) :
    GraphicalModels.CondIndep
        (latentObsJointLaw P F (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov))
        (fun z => z.2 i) (fun z => z.2 j) Prod.fst := by
  set K := measurementKernel P (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov) with hKdef
  have hmi : Measurable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) => x i) := by fun_prop
  have hmj : Measurable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) => x j) := by fun_prop
  have hmij : Measurable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) => (x i, x j)) := hmi.prodMk hmj
  refine ⟨K.map (fun x => x i), K.map (fun x => x j),
    Kernel.IsMarkovKernel.map _ hmi, Kernel.IsMarkovKernel.map _ hmj, ?_⟩
  -- the measurement kernel, read pairwise, *is* the product of its two coordinate marginals
  have hK : K.map (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) => (x i, x j))
      = (K.map fun x => x i) ×ₖ (K.map fun x => x j) := by
    refine Kernel.ext fun y => ?_
    rw [Kernel.map_apply _ hmij, Kernel.prod_apply, Kernel.map_apply _ hmi,
      Kernel.map_apply _ hmj]
    exact (indepFun_iff_map_prod_eq_prod_map_map hmi.aemeasurable hmj.aemeasurable).1
      (indepFun_eval_measurementKernel P hΨdiag hΨ hij y)
  have hfst : (latentObsJointLaw P F (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)).map Prod.fst = F := by
    rw [latentObsJointLaw, ← Measure.fst, Measure.fst_compProd]
  calc (latentObsJointLaw P F (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)).map
        (fun z => (z.1, (z.2 i, z.2 j)))
      = (F ⊗ₘ K).map (Prod.map id fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) => (x i, x j)) := rfl
    _ = F ⊗ₘ (K.map fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) => (x i, x j)) :=
        (Measure.compProd_map hmij).symm
    _ = F ⊗ₘ ((K.map fun x => x i) ×ₖ (K.map fun x => x j)) := by rw [hK]
    _ = _ := by rw [hfst]
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.GraphicalModels.CondIndep (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.latentObsJointLaw P F (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)) (fun z => z.2.ofLp i) (fun z => z.2.ofLp j) Prod.fst
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.condIndep_eval_latentObsJointLaw
entries.doc:
**HEADLINE — local independence** (`BKM` §1.4, Eq. (1.9); linear-Gaussian instance §3.2,
Eq. (3.1)). In the Gaussian linear factor model with a **diagonal** specific-factor covariance
`Ψ`, two distinct observed coordinates are conditionally independent given the latent factor:
`xᵢ ⫫ xⱼ ∣ y` under the joint law of `(y, x)`.

This is the bridge between the two areas: the conclusion is `GraphicalModels.CondIndep`, the
disintegration predicate of the graphical slice, and the model is `FactorModels.latentObsJointLaw`.
The witnesses `CondIndep` asks for are the two coordinate marginals of the measurement kernel.

*Book vs Lean:* `BKM` Eq. (1.9) states local independence for the whole family and for an
arbitrary conditional density; here it is a **theorem** in the Gaussian linear model, in the
pairwise form that `CondIndep` can express. The family form is
`iIndepFun_eval_measurementKernel` / `map_measurementKernel_eq_pi`, stated at the kernel level
for want of a family conditional-independence predicate.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), P.factorCov.transpose = P.factorCov → StatLean.StatisticalModels.condMeanMatrix (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P) (P.loading * P.factorCov) = P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose * (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)⁻¹
entries.source:
/-- **The posterior mean matrix is `Φ Λᵀ Σ⁻¹`** — Thomson's regression-score matrix
(`BKM` Eq. (3.64); at `Φ = I` this is `Λ′Σ⁻¹`). It is the *same* matrix identity as
Henderson's BLUP matrix `G Zᵀ V⁻¹`. -/
theorem condMeanMatrix_factorScores (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: symmetric latent covariance; BKM Eq. (3.2)
    (hΦ : P.factorCovᵀ = P.factorCov) :
    condMeanMatrix (factorCovariance P) (P.loading * P.factorCov)
      = P.factorCov * P.loadingᵀ * (factorCovariance P)⁻¹ :=
  MixedEffects.condMeanMatrix_lmm (factorDesign P) P.factorCov P.uniqueCov hΦ
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.condMeanMatrix (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P) (P.loading * P.factorCov) = P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose * (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)⁻¹
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.condMeanMatrix_factorScores
entries.doc:
**The posterior mean matrix is `Φ Λᵀ Σ⁻¹`** — Thomson's regression-score matrix
(`BKM` Eq. (3.64); at `Φ = I` this is `Λ′Σ⁻¹`). It is the *same* matrix identity as
Henderson's BLUP matrix `G Zᵀ V⁻¹`.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), P.factorCov.PosDef → P.uniqueCov.PosDef → P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose * (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)⁻¹ = (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gammaMatrix P + P.factorCov⁻¹)⁻¹ * P.loading.transpose * P.uniqueCov⁻¹
entries.source:
/-- **`BKM` Eq. (3.7)–(3.8), general `Φ`** — the covariance form of the factor-score matrix
equals its precision form. This is **exactly** Henderson's push-through identity
(`Hen50`; Searle–Casella–McCulloch §7.6) at `Z = Λ`, `G = Φ`, `R = Ψ`. -/
theorem condMeanMatrix_factorScores_precision (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: positive-definite variance components (both inverses must exist);
    -- BKM Eq. (3.7)–(3.8)
    (hΦ : P.factorCov.PosDef) (hΨ : P.uniqueCov.PosDef) :
    P.factorCov * P.loadingᵀ * (factorCovariance P)⁻¹
      = (gammaMatrix P + P.factorCov⁻¹)⁻¹ * P.loadingᵀ * P.uniqueCov⁻¹ :=
  MixedEffects.pushThrough P.loading P.factorCov P.uniqueCov hΦ hΨ
entries.result: P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose * (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)⁻¹ = (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gammaMatrix P + P.factorCov⁻¹)⁻¹ * P.loading.transpose * P.uniqueCov⁻¹
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.condMeanMatrix_factorScores_precision
entries.doc:
**`BKM` Eq. (3.7)–(3.8), general `Φ`** — the covariance form of the factor-score matrix
equals its precision form. This is **exactly** Henderson's push-through identity
(`Hen50`; Searle–Casella–McCulloch §7.6) at `Z = Λ`, `G = Φ`, `R = Ψ`.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.IsStandardized P → P.uniqueCov.PosDef → P.loading.transpose * (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)⁻¹ = (1 + StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gammaMatrix P)⁻¹ * P.loading.transpose * P.uniqueCov⁻¹
entries.source:
/-- **`BKM` Eq. (3.64) verbatim** — at the book's normalization `Φ = I`, the regression-score
matrix is `C = Λ′Σ⁻¹ = (I + Γ)⁻¹Λ′Ψ⁻¹`. The `Φ = I` case of
`condMeanMatrix_factorScores_precision`. -/
theorem condMeanMatrix_factorScores_standardized (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: BKM's normalization y ∼ N_q(0, I); BKM Eq. (3.2)
    (hP : IsStandardized P)
    -- USER-INPUT: nonsingular specific-factor covariance; BKM Eq. (3.64)
    (hΨ : P.uniqueCov.PosDef) :
    P.loadingᵀ * (factorCovariance P)⁻¹
      = (1 + gammaMatrix P)⁻¹ * P.loadingᵀ * P.uniqueCov⁻¹ := by
  have hΦ : P.factorCov.PosDef := by rw [hP]; exact Matrix.PosDef.one
  have h := condMeanMatrix_factorScores_precision P hΦ hΨ
  rw [hP, inv_one, Matrix.one_mul, add_comm (gammaMatrix P) 1] at h
  exact h
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.condMeanMatrix_factorScores_standardized
entries.doc:
**`BKM` Eq. (3.64) verbatim** — at the book's normalization `Φ = I`, the regression-score
matrix is `C = Λ′Σ⁻¹ = (I + Γ)⁻¹Λ′Ψ⁻¹`. The `Φ = I` case of
`condMeanMatrix_factorScores_precision`.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) (F : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))) (E : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))) [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure F] [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure E], MeasureTheory.MemLp id 2 F → MeasureTheory.MemLp id 2 E → StatLean.StatisticalModels.covMatrix (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P F E) = P.loading * StatLean.StatisticalModels.covMatrix F * P.loading.transpose + StatLean.StatisticalModels.covMatrix E
entries.source:
/-- **Second moment, latent form** (`LW82` Eq. (1.2) at `Z = Λ`): the observed covariance is
`Λ · Cov(y) · Λᵀ + Cov(e)`, for **arbitrary** latent and error laws. The covariance
decomposition of `BKM` Eq. (3.12) is its special case at laws carrying `(Φ, Ψ)`. -/
theorem covMatrix_factorLaw (P : FactorParams p q) (F : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)))
    (E : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))) [IsProbabilityMeasure F]
    [IsProbabilityMeasure E]
    -- USER-INPUT: second moments of the latent and specific factors; BKM Eq. (3.2)–(3.3)
    (hF2 : MemLp id 2 F) (hE2 : MemLp id 2 E) :
    covMatrix (factorLaw P F E)
      = P.loading * covMatrix F * P.loadingᵀ + covMatrix E := by
  rw [factorLaw_eq_lmmLaw, MixedEffects.covMatrix_lmmLaw (factorDesign P) P.μ F E hF2 hE2,
    factorDesign_Z]
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.covMatrix (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P F E) = P.loading * StatLean.StatisticalModels.covMatrix F * P.loading.transpose + StatLean.StatisticalModels.covMatrix E
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.covMatrix_factorLaw
entries.doc:
**Second moment, latent form** (`LW82` Eq. (1.2) at `Z = Λ`): the observed covariance is
`Λ · Cov(y) · Λᵀ + Cov(e)`, for **arbitrary** latent and error laws. The covariance
decomposition of `BKM` Eq. (3.12) is its special case at laws carrying `(Φ, Ψ)`.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) (F : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))) (E : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))) [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure F] [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure E], StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.RealizesFactorParams P F E → MeasureTheory.MemLp id 2 F → MeasureTheory.MemLp id 2 E → StatLean.StatisticalModels.covMatrix (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P F E) = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P
entries.source:
/-- **HEADLINE — the factor-analytic covariance decomposition** (`BKM` Eq. (3.12), general
`Φ`): `Σ = Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ`, for latent and specific laws realizing `(Φ, Ψ)`. -/
theorem covMatrix_factorLaw_eq_factorCovariance (P : FactorParams p q)
    (F : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))) (E : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)))
    [IsProbabilityMeasure F] [IsProbabilityMeasure E]
    -- USER-INPUT: the free laws carry the declared parameters; BKM Eq. (3.2)–(3.3)
    (hPFE : RealizesFactorParams P F E)
    -- USER-INPUT: second moments exist; BKM Eq. (3.3)
    (hF2 : MemLp id 2 F) (hE2 : MemLp id 2 E) :
    covMatrix (factorLaw P F E) = factorCovariance P := by
  rw [covMatrix_factorLaw P F E hF2 hE2, hPFE.covMatrix_latent, hPFE.covMatrix_error,
    factorCovariance_eq]
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.covMatrix_factorLaw_eq_factorCovariance
entries.doc:
**HEADLINE — the factor-analytic covariance decomposition** (`BKM` Eq. (3.12), general
`Φ`): `Σ = Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ`, for latent and specific laws realizing `(Φ, Ψ)`.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.IsProperFactorParams P → StatLean.StatisticalModels.covMatrix (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianFactorModel p q P) = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P
entries.source:
/-- The covariance of the Gaussian factor model is `Σ = Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ` (`BKM` Eq. (3.12),
general `Φ`). -/
theorem covMatrix_gaussianFactorModel (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: genuine covariance parameters; BKM Eq. (3.1)–(3.2)
    (hP : IsProperFactorParams P) :
    covMatrix (gaussianFactorModel p q P) = factorCovariance P := by
  rw [gaussianFactorModel_eq_multivariateGaussian P hP]
  exact covMatrix_multivariateGaussian _ _ (posSemidef_factorCovariance P hP)
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.covMatrix_gaussianFactorModel
entries.doc:
The covariance of the Gaussian factor model is `Σ = Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ` (`BKM` Eq. (3.12),
general `Φ`).

entries.statement: {p q : ℕ} → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q → Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ
entries.source:
/-- The **factor covariance** `Σ = Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ` (`BKM` Eq. (3.12) at `Φ = I`; the general `Φ`
is our generalization). This is a *parameter-side* definition: that it is the covariance
matrix of `factorLaw` is `FactorModels.Moments.covMatrix_factorLaw_eq_factorCovariance`. -/
noncomputable def factorCovariance (P : FactorParams p q) : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ :=
  P.loading * P.factorCov * P.loadingᵀ + P.uniqueCov
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance
entries.doc:
The **factor covariance** `Σ = Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ` (`BKM` Eq. (3.12) at `Φ = I`; the general `Φ`
is our generalization). This is a *parameter-side* definition: that it is the covariance
matrix of `factorLaw` is `FactorModels.Moments.covMatrix_factorLaw_eq_factorCovariance`.

entries.statement: ∀ {p : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p 1), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.IsStandardized P → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.HasDiagonalUniqueness P → ∀ {i j : Fin p}, i ≠ j → P.loading i 0 ≠ 0 → P.loading j 0 ≠ 0 → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P i j ≠ 0
entries.source:
/-- **The common factor induces observed correlation** (`BKM` §1.4, p. 7: "if `x₁` and `x₂` both
depend on `y₁` we may expect the common influence of `y₁` to induce a correlation between `x₁`
and `x₂`"). For a standardized one-factor model, the observed covariance between two
coordinates with non-zero loadings is non-zero — despite their conditional independence given
the factor. -/
theorem factorCovariance_apply_ne_zero_of_oneFactor (P : FactorParams p 1)
    -- USER-INPUT: standardized latent factor, `Φ = I`; BKM Eq. (3.2)
    (hΦ : IsStandardized P)
    -- USER-INPUT: `Ψ` diagonal; BKM Eq. (3.1)
    (hΨdiag : HasDiagonalUniqueness P) {i j : Fin p}
    -- USER-INPUT: two distinct observed coordinates; BKM Eq. (3.12)
    (hij : i ≠ j)
    -- USER-INPUT: coordinate `i` genuinely loads on the factor; BKM §1.4, p. 7
    (hi : P.loading i 0 ≠ 0)
    -- USER-INPUT: coordinate `j` genuinely loads on the same factor; BKM §1.4, p. 7
    (hj : P.loading j 0 ≠ 0) :
    factorCovariance P i j ≠ 0 := by
  rw [factorCovariance_apply_of_oneFactor P hΨdiag hij, show P.factorCov = 1 from hΦ]
  simp only [Matrix.one_apply_eq, mul_one]
  exact mul_ne_zero hi hj
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance_apply_ne_zero_of_oneFactor
entries.doc:
**The common factor induces observed correlation** (`BKM` §1.4, p. 7: "if `x₁` and `x₂` both
depend on `y₁` we may expect the common influence of `y₁` to induce a correlation between `x₁`
and `x₂`"). For a standardized one-factor model, the observed covariance between two
coordinates with non-zero loadings is non-zero — despite their conditional independence given
the factor.

entries.statement: ∀ {p : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p 1), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.HasDiagonalUniqueness P → ∀ {i j : Fin p}, i ≠ j → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P i j = P.loading i 0 * P.factorCov 0 0 * P.loading j 0
entries.source:
/-- The **off-diagonal entries of the one-factor covariance**: for `q = 1` and `Ψ` diagonal,
`Σᵢⱼ = λᵢ φ λⱼ` whenever `i ≠ j` — the specific factors drop out entirely off the diagonal
(contrast `Communality.variance_eq_common_add_specificVariance`, which is the diagonal
case). -/
theorem factorCovariance_apply_of_oneFactor (P : FactorParams p 1)
    -- USER-INPUT: `Ψ` diagonal — the factor-analytic restriction; BKM Eq. (3.1), (3.12)
    (hΨdiag : HasDiagonalUniqueness P) {i j : Fin p}
    -- USER-INPUT: two distinct observed coordinates; BKM Eq. (3.12)
    (hij : i ≠ j) :
    factorCovariance P i j = P.loading i 0 * P.factorCov 0 0 * P.loading j 0 := by
  simp [factorCovariance, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply,
    hΨdiag hij]
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P i j = P.loading i 0 * P.factorCov 0 0 * P.loading j 0
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance_apply_of_oneFactor
entries.doc:
The **off-diagonal entries of the one-factor covariance**: for `q = 1` and `Ψ` diagonal,
`Σᵢⱼ = λᵢ φ λⱼ` whenever `i ≠ j` — the specific factors drop out entirely off the diagonal
(contrast `Communality.variance_eq_common_add_specificVariance`, which is the diagonal
case).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P = P.loading * P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose + P.uniqueCov
entries.source:
theorem factorCovariance_eq (P : FactorParams p q) :
    factorCovariance P = P.loading * P.factorCov * P.loadingᵀ + P.uniqueCov := rfl
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance_eq

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.commonCovariance P + P.uniqueCov
entries.source:
theorem factorCovariance_eq_commonCovariance_add (P : FactorParams p q) :
    factorCovariance P = commonCovariance P + P.uniqueCov := rfl
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance_eq_commonCovariance_add

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.IsStandardized P → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P = P.loading * P.loading.transpose + P.uniqueCov
entries.source:
/-- `BKM` Eq. (3.12) verbatim: for **standardized** factors (`Φ = I`, the book's own
normalization at Eq. (3.2)) the decomposition reads `Σ = Λ Λ′ + Ψ`. -/
theorem factorCovariance_of_isStandardized (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: BKM's normalization y ∼ N_q(0, I); BKM Eq. (3.2)
    (hP : IsStandardized P) :
    factorCovariance P = P.loading * P.loadingᵀ + P.uniqueCov := by
  rw [factorCovariance_eq, hP, Matrix.mul_one]
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance_of_isStandardized
entries.doc:
`BKM` Eq. (3.12) verbatim: for **standardized** factors (`Φ = I`, the book's own
normalization at Eq. (3.2)) the decomposition reads `Σ = Λ Λ′ + Ψ`.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}, IsUnit A.det → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.rotateParams P A) = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P
entries.source:
/-- **The factor covariance is rotation invariant**: `Σ` does not change under any
nonsingular reparameterization of the latent space (`BKM` §2.11, Eq. (2.26); §3.13). -/
theorem factorCovariance_rotateParams (P : FactorParams p q)
    {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}
    -- USER-INPUT: the reparameterization is a change of basis of the latent space;
    -- BKM §2.11
    (hA : IsUnit A.det) :
    factorCovariance (rotateParams P A) = factorCovariance P := by
  rw [factorCovariance_eq_commonCovariance_add, factorCovariance_eq_commonCovariance_add,
    commonCovariance_rotateParams P hA, rotateParams_uniqueCov]
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance_rotateParams
entries.doc:
**The factor covariance is rotation invariant**: `Σ` does not change under any
nonsingular reparameterization of the latent space (`BKM` §2.11, Eq. (2.26); §3.13).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) {Q : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}, Q * Q.transpose = 1 → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.rotateParams P Q) = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P
entries.source:
/-- **The book's orthogonal-rotation statement** (`BKM` §3.13.1): for standardized factors,
`Λ` and `Λ Q` give the same covariance `Σ = Λ Λᵀ + Ψ`. -/
theorem factorCovariance_rotateParams_orthogonal (P : FactorParams p q)
    {Q : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}
    -- USER-INPUT: `Q` is orthogonal; BKM §2.11, Eq. (2.24)
    (hQ : Q * Qᵀ = 1) :
    factorCovariance (rotateParams P Q) = factorCovariance P :=
  factorCovariance_rotateParams P (isUnit_det_of_orthogonal hQ)
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance_rotateParams_orthogonal
entries.doc:
**The book's orthogonal-rotation statement** (`BKM` §3.13.1): for standardized factors,
`Λ` and `Λ Q` give the same covariance `Σ = Λ Λᵀ + Ψ`.

entries.statement: {p q : ℕ} → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q → StatLean.StatisticalModels.MixedEffects.LMMDesign p p q
entries.source:
/-- The factor model read as a **linear mixed-effects design**: `X = 1`, `Z = Λ`
(`LW82` Eq. (1.1) instantiated at `BKM` Eq. (3.3)). -/
def factorDesign (P : FactorParams p q) : MixedEffects.LMMDesign p p q :=
  ⟨1, P.loading⟩
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorDesign
entries.doc:
The factor model read as a **linear mixed-effects design**: `X = 1`, `Z = Λ`

entries.statement: {p q : ℕ} → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q → MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)) → MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) → MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))
entries.source:
/-- The **joint law of `(x, y)`** — observation block first, latent factors second (the block
order at which `Gaussian.Conditioning` applies without a swap). Defined as the mixed-model
joint law of the factor design. -/
noncomputable def factorJointLaw (P : FactorParams p q)
    (F : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))) (E : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))) :
    Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)) :=
  MixedEffects.lmmJointLaw (factorDesign P) P.μ F E
entries.result: MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorJointLaw
entries.doc:
The **joint law of `(x, y)`** — observation block first, latent factors second (the block
order at which `Gaussian.Conditioning` applies without a swap). Defined as the mixed-model
joint law of the factor design.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), P.factorCov.PosSemidef → P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorJointLaw P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov) = MeasureTheory.Measure.map (⇑StatLean.StatisticalModels.sumMeasEquivProd) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (StatLean.StatisticalModels.blockPair P.μ 0) (Matrix.fromBlocks (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P) (P.loading * P.factorCov) (P.loading * P.factorCov).transpose P.factorCov))
entries.source:
/-- **The Gaussian joint law** (`BKM` Eq. (3.1)–(3.3) jointly): `(x, y)` is the block Gaussian
with `Σ_xx = Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ`, `Σ_xy = Λ Φ` and `Σ_yy = Φ`. -/
theorem factorJointLaw_eq_blockGaussian (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: genuine covariance parameters; BKM Eq. (3.1)–(3.2)
    (hΦ : P.factorCov.PosSemidef) (hΨ : P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef) :
    factorJointLaw P (multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov)
        (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)
      = (multivariateGaussian (blockPair P.μ 0)
          (Matrix.fromBlocks (factorCovariance P) (P.loading * P.factorCov)
            (P.loading * P.factorCov)ᵀ P.factorCov)).map
            (sumMeasEquivProd (ι₁ := Fin p) (ι₂ := Fin q)) := by
  rw [factorJointLaw, MixedEffects.lmmJointLaw_eq_blockGaussian _ _ _ _ hΦ hΨ,
    factorDesign_X, toEuclideanLin_one_apply]
  rfl
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorJointLaw P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov) = MeasureTheory.Measure.map (⇑StatLean.StatisticalModels.sumMeasEquivProd) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (StatLean.StatisticalModels.blockPair P.μ 0) (Matrix.fromBlocks (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P) (P.loading * P.factorCov) (P.loading * P.factorCov).transpose P.factorCov))

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) (F : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))) (E : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))) [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure F] [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure E], MeasureTheory.Measure.map Prod.fst (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorJointLaw P F E) = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P F E

/-- The observation marginal of the joint law is the factor model's observed law. -/
theorem factorJointLaw_fst (P : FactorParams p q)
    (F : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))) (E : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)))
    [IsProbabilityMeasure F] [IsProbabilityMeasure E] :
    (factorJointLaw P F E).map Prod.fst = factorLaw P F E := by
  rw [factorJointLaw, MixedEffects.lmmJointLaw_fst, factorLaw_eq_lmmLaw]

entries.statement: {p q : ℕ} → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q → MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)) → MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) → MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))
entries.source:
/-- The **observed law of the linear factor model** (`BKM` Eq. (3.3)/(3.5)): the latent law
`F` marginalized through the measurement kernel, i.e. the law of `x = μ + Λ y + e` with
`y ∼ F` and `e ∼ E` independent. The latent and error laws are free parameters; Gaussianity
enters only in `FactorModels.Gaussian`.

*Edge behavior:* a probability measure exactly when `F` and `E` are (instance below); for
non-s-finite arguments this is the usual `Measure.bind` junk. -/
noncomputable def factorLaw (P : FactorParams p q) (F : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)))
    (E : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))) : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) :=
  measurementKernel P E ∘ₘ F

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) (F : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))) (E : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))) [MeasureTheory.SFinite F] [MeasureTheory.SFinite E], StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P F E = StatLean.StatisticalModels.MixedEffects.lmmLaw (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorDesign P) P.μ F E
entries.source:
/-- **The bridge**: the linear factor model is the linear mixed model with `X = 1`, `β = μ`,
`Z = Λ` (`BKM` Eq. (3.3) = `LW82` Eq. (1.1)). -/
theorem factorLaw_eq_lmmLaw (P : FactorParams p q) (F : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)))
    (E : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)))
    -- LEAN-ONLY: s-finiteness of both free laws; without it `Measure.bind` and
    -- `Measure.prod` are junk on both sides and the identity carries no content
    [SFinite F] [SFinite E] :
    factorLaw P F E = MixedEffects.lmmLaw (factorDesign P) P.μ F E := by
  have hA : Measurable fun y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q) =>
      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) P.loading y :=
    ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) P.loading).continuous_of_finiteDimensional).measurable
  have hg : Measurable fun be : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) =>
      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) (factorDesign P).X P.μ
        + Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) (factorDesign P).Z be.1 + be.2 :=
    ((hA.comp measurable_fst).const_add _).add measurable_snd
  -- both sides are `∫⁻ y, E {z ∣ Λ y + μ + z ∈ s} ∂F`: `Measure.bind_apply` on the left,
  -- `Measure.prod_apply` on the right; the integrands differ only by `add_comm`
  ext s hs
  rw [factorLaw, MixedEffects.lmmLaw,
    Measure.bind_apply hs (Kernel.measurable _).aemeasurable,
    Measure.map_apply hg hs, Measure.prod_apply (hg hs)]
  refine lintegral_congr fun y => ?_
  rw [measurementKernel_apply, Measure.map_apply (by fun_prop) hs]
  congr 1
  ext z
  simp only [Set.mem_preimage, factorDesign_X, factorDesign_Z, toEuclideanLin_one_apply]
  rw [add_comm (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) P.loading y) P.μ]
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P F E = StatLean.StatisticalModels.MixedEffects.lmmLaw (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorDesign P) P.μ F E
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw_eq_lmmLaw
entries.doc:
**The bridge**: the linear factor model is the linear mixed model with `X = 1`, `β = μ`,

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.IsProperFactorParams P → (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P).PosDef → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov) = MeasureTheory.volume.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik P x))
entries.source:
/-- **The density theorem** — the observed law of the normal factor model has
`exp (factorLogLik P ·)` as its Lebesgue density, i.e. `factorLogLik` really is the
observed-data log-likelihood and not merely a formula named after one (`BKM` Eq. (3.5)). -/
theorem factorLaw_eq_withDensity_exp_factorLogLik (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: genuine covariance parameters; BKM Eq. (3.1)–(3.2)
    (hP : IsProperFactorParams P)
    -- USER-INPUT: nondegenerate observed covariance — a singular Σ has no Lebesgue
    -- density at all; BKM Eq. (3.5)
    (hSig : (factorCovariance P).PosDef) :
    factorLaw P (multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)
      = volume.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (factorLogLik P x)) := by
  rw [factorLaw_multivariateGaussian P hP.1 hP.2]
  exact multivariateGaussian_eq_withDensity_exp_gaussianLogDensity p P.μ hSig
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov) = MeasureTheory.volume.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik P x))
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw_eq_withDensity_exp_factorLogLik
entries.doc:

`exp (factorLogLik P ·)` as its Lebesgue density, i.e. `factorLogLik` really is the
observed-data log-likelihood and not merely a formula named after one (`BKM` Eq. (3.5)).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), P.factorCov.PosSemidef → P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov) = ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian P.μ (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)
entries.source:
/-- **HEADLINE — `BKM` Eq. (3.5), general `Φ`**: the Gaussian factor model has observed law
`x ∼ N_p(μ, Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ)`. -/
theorem factorLaw_multivariateGaussian (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: genuine covariance parameters; BKM Eq. (3.1)–(3.2)
    (hΦ : P.factorCov.PosSemidef) (hΨ : P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef) :
    factorLaw P (multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)
      = multivariateGaussian P.μ (factorCovariance P) := by
  rw [factorLaw_eq_lmmLaw, MixedEffects.lmmLaw_multivariateGaussian _ _ _ _ hΦ hΨ,
    factorDesign_X, toEuclideanLin_one_apply]
  rfl
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov) = ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian P.μ (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw_multivariateGaussian
entries.doc:
**HEADLINE — `BKM` Eq. (3.5), general `Φ`**: the Gaussian factor model has observed law
`x ∼ N_p(μ, Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ)`.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) (F : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))) (E : MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))) {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}, IsUnit A.det → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.rotateParams P A) (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun y => (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A⁻¹) y) F) E = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P F E
entries.source:
/-- **The observed law is rotation invariant** — the exact statement, with the latent law
transported along with the parameters: `y ↦ A⁻¹ y` turns a draw from `F` into a draw from the
rotated latent law, and the two observed models coincide. No moment or Gaussianity
hypothesis is needed. -/
theorem factorLaw_rotateParams (P : FactorParams p q)
    (F : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))) (E : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)))
    {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}
    -- USER-INPUT: the reparameterization is a change of basis of the latent space;
    -- BKM §2.11
    (hA : IsUnit A.det) :
    factorLaw (rotateParams P A)
        (F.map fun y => Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) A⁻¹ y) E
      = factorLaw P F E := by
  have hg : Measurable fun y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q) =>
      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) A⁻¹ y :=
    ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) A⁻¹).continuous_of_finiteDimensional).measurable
  -- the loading of the rotated tuple undoes the transport of the latent variable
  have hLA : ∀ y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q),
      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) (rotateParams P A).loading
          (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) A⁻¹ y)
        = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) P.loading y := by
    intro y
    have key : (P.loading * A) *ᵥ (A⁻¹ *ᵥ (WithLp.ofLp y))
        = P.loading *ᵥ (WithLp.ofLp y) := by
      rw [Matrix.mulVec_mulVec, Matrix.mul_nonsing_inv_cancel_right _ _ hA]
    exact congrArg (WithLp.toLp 2) key
  -- hence the two measurement kernels agree along the transport
  have hker : ∀ y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q),
      measurementKernel (rotateParams P A) E (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ) A⁻¹ y)
        = measurementKernel P E y := by
    intro y
    by_cases hE : SFinite E
    · rw [measurementKernel_apply, measurementKernel_apply, hLA y, rotateParams_μ]
    · -- LEAN-ONLY: junk regime — without `SFinite E` the product kernel, hence the
      -- measurement kernel, is `0` on both sides
      have hns : ¬ IsSFiniteKernel (Kernel.const (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)) E) := by
        rw [Kernel.isSFiniteKernel_const]; exact hE
      simp [measurementKernel, affineNoiseKernel,
        Kernel.prod_of_not_isSFiniteKernel_right _ hns]
  ext s hs
  rw [factorLaw, factorLaw, Measure.bind_apply hs (Kernel.aemeasurable _),
    Measure.bind_apply hs (Kernel.aemeasurable _),
    lintegral_map (Kernel.measurable_coe _ hs) hg]
  exact lintegral_congr fun y => by rw [hker y]
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.rotateParams P A) (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun y => (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A⁻¹) y) F) E = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P F E
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw_rotateParams
entries.doc:

rotated latent law, and the two observed models coincide. No moment or Gaussianity
hypothesis is needed.

entries.statement: {p q : ℕ} → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) → ℝ
entries.source:
/-- The **observed-data log-likelihood contribution** of the normal factor model at a single
observation `x` (`BKM` Eq. (3.5) with Eq. (3.12)): the multivariate normal log density at the
structured covariance `Σ = Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ`. The latent factors are already integrated out — this
is not a complete-data likelihood. -/
noncomputable def factorLogLik (P : FactorParams p q) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) : ℝ :=
  gaussianLogDensity P.μ (factorCovariance P) x
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik
entries.doc:
The **observed-data log-likelihood contribution** of the normal factor model at a single
observation `x` (`BKM` Eq. (3.5) with Eq. (3.12)): the multivariate normal log density at the
structured covariance `Σ = Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ`. The latent factors are already integrated out — this
is not a complete-data likelihood.

entries.statement: {p q n : ℕ} → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q → (Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) → ℝ
entries.source:
/-- The **log-likelihood of an i.i.d. sample** `x₁, …, x_n` (`BKM` §3.4). -/
noncomputable def factorLogLikSample {n : ℕ} (P : FactorParams p q)
    (x : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, factorLogLik P (x i)
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLikSample
entries.doc: The **log-likelihood of an i.i.d. sample** `x₁, …, x_n` (`BKM` §3.4).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q n : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}, IsUnit A.det → ∀ (x : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLikSample (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.rotateParams P A) x = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLikSample P x
entries.source:
/-- The sample log-likelihood inherits rotation invariance. -/
theorem factorLogLikSample_rotateParams {n : ℕ} (P : FactorParams p q)
    {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}
    -- USER-INPUT: the reparameterization is a change of basis of the latent space;
    -- BKM §2.11
    (hA : IsUnit A.det) (x : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) :
    factorLogLikSample (rotateParams P A) x = factorLogLikSample P x :=
  Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => factorLogLik_rotateParams P hA (x i)
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLikSample_rotateParams
entries.doc: The sample log-likelihood inherits rotation invariance.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P P' : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), P.μ = P'.μ → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P' → ∀ (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik P x = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik P' x
entries.source:
/-- The likelihood sees the parameters only through `(μ, Σ)` — definitional, and the reason
every invariance below is a one-line corollary. -/
theorem factorLogLik_congr (P P' : FactorParams p q)
    -- LEAN-ONLY: the two parameter tuples agree on the pair the density depends on;
    -- antecedent, no scope change
    (hμ : P.μ = P'.μ) (hSig : factorCovariance P = factorCovariance P')
    (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) :
    factorLogLik P x = factorLogLik P' x := by
  rw [factorLogLik_eq_gaussianLogDensity, factorLogLik_eq_gaussianLogDensity, hμ, hSig]
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik_congr
entries.doc:
The likelihood sees the parameters only through `(μ, Σ)` — definitional, and the reason
every invariance below is a one-line corollary.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik P x = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianLogDensity P.μ (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P) x
entries.source:
theorem factorLogLik_eq_gaussianLogDensity (P : FactorParams p q)
    (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) :
    factorLogLik P x = gaussianLogDensity P.μ (factorCovariance P) x := rfl
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik_eq_gaussianLogDensity

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}, IsUnit A.det → ∀ (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.rotateParams P A) x = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik P x
entries.source:
/-- **HEADLINE — the likelihood is rotation invariant** (`BKM` §3.3, p. 50; §3.13.1): every
nonsingular reparameterization `Λ ↦ Λ A`, `Φ ↦ A⁻¹ Φ A⁻ᵀ` of the latent space leaves the
observed-data log-likelihood unchanged, because it leaves `Σ` unchanged. This is why maximum
likelihood determines `Λ` only up to rotation and why an identifying restriction
(`BKM`: `Λ′Ψ⁻¹Λ` diagonal) must be imposed. -/
theorem factorLogLik_rotateParams (P : FactorParams p q) {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}
    -- USER-INPUT: the reparameterization is a change of basis of the latent space;
    -- BKM §2.11
    (hA : IsUnit A.det) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) :
    factorLogLik (rotateParams P A) x = factorLogLik P x :=
  factorLogLik_congr (rotateParams P A) P rfl (factorCovariance_rotateParams P hA) x
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik_rotateParams
entries.doc:
**HEADLINE — the likelihood is rotation invariant** (`BKM` §3.3, p. 50; §3.13.1): every
nonsingular reparameterization `Λ ↦ Λ A`, `Φ ↦ A⁻¹ Φ A⁻ᵀ` of the latent space leaves the
observed-data log-likelihood unchanged, because it leaves `Σ` unchanged. This is why maximum
likelihood determines `Λ` only up to rotation and why an identifying restriction
(`BKM`: `Λ′Ψ⁻¹Λ` diagonal) must be imposed.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) {Q : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}, Q * Q.transpose = 1 → ∀ (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.rotateParams P Q) x = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik P x
entries.source:
/-- **Orthogonal rotations leave the likelihood unchanged** — the statement `BKM` §3.13.1
makes for standardized factors. -/
theorem factorLogLik_rotateParams_orthogonal (P : FactorParams p q)
    {Q : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}
    -- USER-INPUT: `Q` is orthogonal; BKM §2.11, Eq. (2.24)
    (hQ : Q * Qᵀ = 1) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) :
    factorLogLik (rotateParams P Q) x = factorLogLik P x :=
  factorLogLik_congr (rotateParams P Q) P rfl
    (factorCovariance_rotateParams_orthogonal P hQ) x
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLogLik_rotateParams_orthogonal
entries.doc:
**Orthogonal rotations leave the likelihood unchanged** — the statement `BKM` §3.13.1
makes for standardized factors.

entries.statement: {p q : ℕ} → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q → ProbabilityTheory.Kernel (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q))
entries.source:
/-- The **factor-score kernel** `x ↦ law of (y ∣ x)` (`BKM` Eq. (3.6)): the Gaussian
conditional kernel at the factor model's blocks. Its mean and covariance are computed by
`factorScoreKernel_apply` below.

*Edge behavior:* inherits `gaussianCondKernel`'s unconditional Markov property; at a singular
`Σ` the `Matrix.inv` junk value (`0`) makes the mean function `0`, hence the `PosDef`
hypotheses downstream. -/
noncomputable def factorScoreKernel (P : FactorParams p q) :
    Kernel (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)) :=
  gaussianCondKernel P.μ 0 (factorCovariance P) (P.loading * P.factorCov) P.factorCov
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorScoreKernel
entries.doc:
The **factor-score kernel** `x ↦ law of (y ∣ x)` (`BKM` Eq. (3.6)): the Gaussian
conditional kernel at the factor model's blocks. Its mean and covariance are computed by
`factorScoreKernel_apply` below.

*Edge behavior:* inherits `gaussianCondKernel`'s unconditional Markov property; at a singular
`Σ` the `Matrix.inv` junk value (`0`) makes the mean function `0`, hence the `PosDef`
hypotheses downstream.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), P.factorCov.transpose = P.factorCov → ∀ (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)), (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorScoreKernel P) x = ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin (P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose * (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)⁻¹)) (x - P.μ)) (P.factorCov - P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose * (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)⁻¹ * P.loading * P.factorCov)
entries.source:
/-- **HEADLINE — the posterior law of the factors** (`BKM` Eq. (3.6), general `Φ`):
`y ∣ x ∼ N_q(Φ Λᵀ Σ⁻¹ (x − μ), Φ − Φ Λᵀ Σ⁻¹ Λ Φ)`. -/
theorem factorScoreKernel_apply (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: symmetric latent covariance; BKM Eq. (3.2)
    (hΦ : P.factorCovᵀ = P.factorCov) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) :
    factorScoreKernel P x
      = multivariateGaussian
          (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := ℝ)
            (P.factorCov * P.loadingᵀ * (factorCovariance P)⁻¹) (x - P.μ))
          (P.factorCov
            - P.factorCov * P.loadingᵀ * (factorCovariance P)⁻¹ * P.loading
                * P.factorCov) := by
  rw [factorScoreKernel, gaussianCondKernel_apply, condMeanMatrix_factorScores P hΦ,
    condCovMatrix_factorScores P hΦ, zero_add]
entries.result: (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorScoreKernel P) x = ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin (P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose * (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)⁻¹)) (x - P.μ)) (P.factorCov - P.factorCov * P.loading.transpose * (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)⁻¹ * P.loading * P.factorCov)
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorScoreKernel_apply
entries.doc:
**HEADLINE — the posterior law of the factors** (`BKM` Eq. (3.6), general `Φ`):
`y ∣ x ∼ N_q(Φ Λᵀ Σ⁻¹ (x − μ), Φ − Φ Λᵀ Σ⁻¹ Λ Φ)`.

entries.statement: {p q : ℕ} → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q → Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ
entries.source:
/-- `BKM`'s `Γ = Λ′Ψ⁻¹Λ` (`BKM` Eq. (3.9)). **Symbol warning:** in `BKM` ch. 3, `Γ` is this
matrix and `Φ` denotes the *correlation matrix of the latent variables* (Eq. (3.56)); the two
must not be confused.

*Edge behavior:* `Matrix.inv` is `0` at a singular `Ψ`, in which case `Γ = 0`; the theorems
below carry `Ψ.PosDef`. -/
noncomputable def gammaMatrix (P : FactorParams p q) : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ :=
  P.loadingᵀ * P.uniqueCov⁻¹ * P.loading
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gammaMatrix
entries.doc:

entries.statement: (p q : ℕ) → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q → MeasureTheory.Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))
entries.source:
/-- The **normal linear factor model** as a parameter-to-law map (`BKM` Eq. (3.1)–(3.3)):
Gaussian latent factors `y ∼ N_q(0, Φ)` and Gaussian specific factors `e ∼ N_p(0, Ψ)`.

*Edge behavior:* at parameters with a non-PSD `Φ` or `Ψ` the corresponding
`multivariateGaussian` collapses to a Dirac mass, so the law is **not** `N(μ, Σ)`; all
theorems below assume `IsProperFactorParams`. -/
noncomputable def gaussianFactorModel (p q : ℕ) :
    FactorParams p q → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) :=
  fun P => factorLaw P (multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov)
    (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianFactorModel
entries.doc:

entries.source:

    gaussianFactorModel p q P
      = factorLaw P (multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov)
          (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov) := rfl
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianFactorModel p q P = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorLaw P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.factorCov) (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.IsProperFactorParams P → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianFactorModel p q P = ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian P.μ (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)
entries.source:
/-- The model-map form of the headline. -/
theorem gaussianFactorModel_eq_multivariateGaussian (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: genuine covariance parameters; BKM Eq. (3.1)–(3.2)
    (hP : IsProperFactorParams P) :
    gaussianFactorModel p q P = multivariateGaussian P.μ (factorCovariance P) := by
  rw [gaussianFactorModel_apply, factorLaw_multivariateGaussian P hP.1 hP.2]
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianFactorModel p q P = ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian P.μ (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance P)
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianFactorModel_eq_multivariateGaussian
entries.doc: The model-map form of the headline.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q) {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}, StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.IsProperFactorParams P → IsUnit A.det → StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianFactorModel p q (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.rotateParams P A) = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianFactorModel p q P
entries.source:
/-- **Rotation invariance of the Gaussian factor model**: in the Gaussian instantiation the
transport of the latent law is automatic (a Gaussian stays Gaussian), so the parameters
`P` and `rotateParams P A` index *literally the same law* — this is the source of the
non-identifiability in `FactorModels.Identifiability`. -/
theorem gaussianFactorModel_rotateParams (P : FactorParams p q)
    {A : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ}
    -- USER-INPUT: genuine covariance parameters; BKM Eq. (3.1)–(3.2)
    (hP : IsProperFactorParams P)
    -- USER-INPUT: the reparameterization is a change of basis of the latent space;
    -- BKM §2.11
    (hA : IsUnit A.det) :
    gaussianFactorModel p q (rotateParams P A) = gaussianFactorModel p q P := by
  rw [gaussianFactorModel_eq_multivariateGaussian _
      (isProperFactorParams_rotateParams P A hP),
    gaussianFactorModel_eq_multivariateGaussian _ hP, rotateParams_μ,
    factorCovariance_rotateParams P hA]
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianFactorModel p q (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.rotateParams P A) = StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianFactorModel p q P
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianFactorModel_rotateParams
entries.doc:
**Rotation invariance of the Gaussian factor model**: in the Gaussian instantiation the

entries.statement: {p : ℕ} → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) → Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) → ℝ
entries.source:
/-- The **multivariate normal log density** at mean `m` and covariance `S`:
`−(p/2) log 2π − ½ log det S − ½ (x−m)ᵀ S⁻¹ (x−m)`.

*Edge behavior:* at a singular `S` this is finite nonsense (`Matrix.det S = 0` with
`Real.log 0 = 0`, and `S⁻¹ = 0`); it represents a density only under `S.PosDef`. -/
noncomputable def gaussianLogDensity (m : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))
    (S : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) : ℝ :=
  -(p / 2 : ℝ) * Real.log (2 * Real.pi) - (1 / 2 : ℝ) * Real.log S.det
    - (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (WithLp.ofLp (x - m) ⬝ᵥ S⁻¹ *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp (x - m))
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.gaussianLogDensity
entries.doc:

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.HasDiagonalUniqueness P → P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef → ∀ (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)), ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i x => x.ofLp i) ((StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.measurementKernel P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)) y)
entries.source:
/-- **`BKM` Eq. (1.9), family form.** All `p` observed coordinates are *jointly* independent
under the conditional law at a fixed factor value — the statement `BKM` actually makes, since
Eq. (1.9) is a product over all `i = 1, …, p`. -/
theorem iIndepFun_eval_measurementKernel (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: `Ψ` diagonal; BKM §3.2 Eq. (3.1)
    (hΨdiag : HasDiagonalUniqueness P)
    -- USER-INPUT: `Ψ` a genuine covariance matrix; BKM Eq. (3.1)
    (hΨ : P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef) (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)) :
    iIndepFun (fun (i : Fin p) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) => x i)
      (measurementKernel P (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov) y) := by
  rw [measurementKernel_multivariateGaussian P hΨ y]
  refine (hasGaussianLaw_coords _ P.uniqueCov).iIndepFun_of_covariance_eq_zero fun i j hij => ?_
  rw [covariance_eval_multivariateGaussian hΨ]
  exact hΨdiag hij
entries.result: ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i x => x.ofLp i) ((StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.measurementKernel P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)) y)
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.iIndepFun_eval_measurementKernel
entries.doc:
**`BKM` Eq. (1.9), family form.** All `p` observed coordinates are *jointly* independent
under the conditional law at a fixed factor value — the statement `BKM` actually makes, since
Eq. (1.9) is a product over all `i = 1, …, p`.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ}, StatLean.StatisticalModels.IdentifiesTarget (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.properGaussianFactorModel p q) fun P => StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.factorCovariance ↑P
entries.source:
/-- **`Σ = Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ` is identified** — it is the covariance matrix of the observed law
(`BKM` Eq. (3.12), general `Φ`). -/
theorem identifiesTarget_factorCovariance :
    IdentifiesTarget (properGaussianFactorModel p q)
      fun P : {P : FactorParams p q // IsProperFactorParams P} => factorCovariance P.1 :=
  identifiesTarget_of_rep covMatrix fun P => covMatrix_gaussianFactorModel P.1 P.2
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.identifiesTarget_factorCovariance
entries.doc:
**`Σ = Λ Φ Λᵀ + Ψ` is identified** — it is the covariance matrix of the observed law
(`BKM` Eq. (3.12), general `Φ`).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (μ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) {Ψ : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ}, Ψ.PosSemidef → StatLean.StatisticalModels.IdentifiesTarget (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.loadingModel p q μ Ψ) fun Λ => Λ * Λ.transpose
entries.source:
/-- **HEADLINE (positive) — the common covariance is identified**: `Λ Λᵀ` is a functional of
the observed law even though `Λ` is not (`BKM` §3.12.1). -/
theorem identifiesTarget_loadingModel_commonCovariance (μ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))
    {Ψ : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ}
    -- USER-INPUT: a genuine specific-factor covariance; BKM Eq. (3.1)
    (hΨ : Ψ.PosSemidef) :
    IdentifiesTarget (loadingModel p q μ Ψ) fun Λ : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin q) ℝ => Λ * Λᵀ := by
  refine identifiesTarget_of_rep (fun Q => covMatrix Q - Ψ) fun Λ => ?_
  simp only [identifiesTarget_loadingModel_covariance_aux μ hΨ Λ, add_sub_cancel_right]
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.IdentifiesTarget (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.loadingModel p q μ Ψ) fun Λ => Λ * Λ.transpose
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.identifiesTarget_loadingModel_commonCovariance
entries.doc:
**HEADLINE (positive) — the common covariance is identified**: `Λ Λᵀ` is a functional of
the observed law even though `Λ` is not (`BKM` §3.12.1).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (μ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p)) {Ψ : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ}, Ψ.PosSemidef → StatLean.StatisticalModels.IdentifiesTarget (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.loadingModel p q μ Ψ) fun Λ => Λ * Λ.transpose + Ψ
entries.source:
/-- The full covariance `Λ Λᵀ + Ψ` is identified in the loading model. -/
theorem identifiesTarget_loadingModel_covariance (μ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p))
    {Ψ : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ}
    -- USER-INPUT: a genuine specific-factor covariance; BKM Eq. (3.1)
    (hΨ : Ψ.PosSemidef) :
    IdentifiesTarget (loadingModel p q μ Ψ)
      fun Λ : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin q) ℝ => Λ * Λᵀ + Ψ :=
  identifiesTarget_of_rep covMatrix (identifiesTarget_loadingModel_covariance_aux μ hΨ)
entries.result: StatLean.StatisticalModels.IdentifiesTarget (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.loadingModel p q μ Ψ) fun Λ => Λ * Λ.transpose + Ψ
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.identifiesTarget_loadingModel_covariance
entries.doc: The full covariance `Λ Λᵀ + Ψ` is identified in the loading model.

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ}, StatLean.StatisticalModels.IdentifiesTarget (StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.properGaussianFactorModel p q) fun P => (↑P).μ
entries.source:
/-- **`μ` is identified** — it is the mean vector of the observed law (`BKM` Eq. (3.5)). -/
theorem identifiesTarget_mean :
    IdentifiesTarget (properGaussianFactorModel p q)
      fun P : {P : FactorParams p q // IsProperFactorParams P} => P.1.μ :=
  identifiesTarget_of_rep meanVec fun P => meanVec_gaussianFactorModel P.1 P.2
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.identifiesTarget_mean
entries.doc: **`μ` is identified** — it is the mean vector of the observed law (`BKM` Eq. (3.5)).

entries.statement: ∀ {p q : ℕ} (P : StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.FactorParams p q), StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.HasDiagonalUniqueness P → P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef → ∀ {i j : Fin p}, i ≠ j → ∀ (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)), ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (fun x => x.ofLp i) (fun x => x.ofLp j) ((StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.measurementKernel P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)) y)
entries.source:
/-- **`BKM` Eq. (1.9), pairwise form.** With Gaussian specific factors and a **diagonal**
specific-factor covariance `Ψ`, two distinct observed coordinates are independent under the
conditional law given the factor — for *every* value `y` of the factor. -/
theorem indepFun_eval_measurementKernel (P : FactorParams p q)
    -- USER-INPUT: the specific factors are uncorrelated across coordinates, i.e. `Ψ` diagonal;
    -- BKM §3.2 Eq. (3.1), the hypothesis that makes Eq. (1.9) hold in the linear model
    (hΨdiag : HasDiagonalUniqueness P)
    -- USER-INPUT: `Ψ` is a genuine covariance matrix; BKM Eq. (3.1). Without it
    -- `multivariateGaussian 0 Ψ` is a Dirac mass and the conditional law is degenerate
    (hΨ : P.uniqueCov.PosSemidef) {i j : Fin p}
    -- USER-INPUT: two distinct observed coordinates; BKM Eq. (1.9)
    (hij : i ≠ j) (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)) :
    IndepFun (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) => x i) (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p) => x j)
      (measurementKernel P (multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov) y) := by
  rw [measurementKernel_multivariateGaussian P hΨ y]
  refine ((hasGaussianLaw_coords _ P.uniqueCov).prodMk i j).indepFun_of_covariance_eq_zero ?_
  rw [covariance_eval_multivariateGaussian hΨ]
  exact hΨdiag hij
entries.result: ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (fun x => x.ofLp i) (fun x => x.ofLp j) ((StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.measurementKernel P (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 P.uniqueCov)) y)
entries.name: StatLean.StatisticalModels.FactorModels.indepFun_eval_measurementKernel
entries.doc:
**`BKM` Eq. (1.9), pairwise form.** With Gaussian specific factors and a **diagonal**
specific-factor covariance `Ψ`, two distinct observed coordinates are independent under the
conditional law given the factor — for *every* value `y` of the factor.
